Paired or independent? Ask this one question
Does each row in one group have a natural partner in the other group?

Same patient, same store, same day — paired. Two unrelated batches of
students, like Section 1’s STEM/Business comparison — independent. Running
the wrong one of

doesn’t
error, so this is a judgment call to make

something R will catch for you.

Why “with continuity correction,” and that warning about small counts

defaults to a continuity-corrected chi-square approximation,
printed right in the header. If your two groups have small counts (R warns

when they do), that
approximation gets shaky — a sign to shrink your claims or use an exact
method instead. The groups above (60 and 60 students) are large enough that
no such warning appears.
